ranked.headline: Spatial omics tools disentangle cell attribution, abundance and state in tissue data
ranked.summary: New methods target attribution errors in spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging: transcripts to cells, pixels to markers, spots to cell types.

ranked.headline: Omics models predict cancer outcomes while glioblastoma and clone dynamics are modeled
ranked.summary: Pre-treatment scRNA-seq, methylation and immune-state models now target toxicity, survival and response, alongside new glioblastoma plasticity maps.

ranked.headline: Perturbation response models chase generalization as benchmarks probe foundation models
ranked.summary: New generative, in-context and cross-modal predictors arrive alongside attribution and baseline benchmarks questioning where foundation models add value.

ranked.headline: Sequence foundation models spread across DNA, RNA and protein as evaluation gets stricter
ranked.summary: New RNA and DNA pretraining (structRFM, LIMBER, IsoAlign) arrives alongside work exposing homology leakage, ligand invariance, and uncalibrated PLM scores.

ranked.headline: Models infer unmeasured protein, chromatin and isoform layers from measured omics
ranked.summary: TSNR and MorphoProt predict spatial protein from RNA, while MUTUAL, IsoPrism and Top2All reconstruct chromatin, isoform and full-transcriptome layers.

ranked.headline: Environment-specific microbial genome catalogs and annotation pipelines enable functional inference
ranked.summary: New plasmid, anaerobic digestion, and proteome-annotation resources, plus long-read strain profiling, extend microbial genomes toward functional inference.

ranked.headline: Sequence-derived microbial identity and function via language models, amplicon typing, and metagenome mining
ranked.summary: Three preprints extend sequence-based typing from DNA language models to TB spoligotyping and metagenome-derived Cas9 PAM profiling.

ranked.headline: Sequence models gain MPRA supervision, 3D context and single-molecule chromatin for variant effects
ranked.summary: Preprints extend sequence-to-function variant scoring with MPRA fine-tuning, single-molecule accessibility and 3D genome inputs, alongside multiomic variant-to-gene atlases.

ranked.headline: Web resources curate sequences, hosts and ligands across toxins, avian flu and plant viruses
ranked.summary: Three new resources link sequence records to structures, hosts, surveillance or antiviral data, with LLM or AI assistance in two of them.

ranked.headline: Curated databases resolve perturbation, isoform, R-loop and drug-response features by cell type
ranked.summary: Several new database releases extend cell-type- and species-resolved annotation to isoforms, R-loops, perturbations and drug sensitivity in a single issue cycle.

ranked.headline: Standardized portals, workflows and knowledge networks consolidate spatial and single-cell omics data
ranked.summary: New portals, harmonised resources and reproducible workflows aim to make spatial and single-cell data searchable, traceable and comparable across cohorts and datasets.

ranked.headline: Pan-cancer dating of whole-genome doubling against drivers, chromosomal losses and immune programmes
ranked.summary: A 41,332-tumour analysis dates whole-genome doubling relative to drivers, losses and immune programmes, alongside somatic mosaicism and variant-calling advances.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks, annotation databases and reference panels extend variant interpretation across coding and non-coding…
ranked.summary: New leakage-controlled benchmarks, domain and membrane-protein resources, and diverse-population references target gaps in variant interpretation and pipeline validation.

ranked.headline: Deep architectures tailored to Hi-C matrices for subcompartments, TAD boundaries and contact enhancement
ranked.summary: Three Hi-C methods adapt model design to contact-matrix structure: single-cell subcompartment calling, compact TAD boundary prediction, and foundation-model-guided enhancement.

ranked.headline: Context-aware filtering and transcript-specific k-mers target mapping ambiguity in isoform quantification
ranked.summary: New preprints refine isoform quantification by modeling long-read MAPQ and isolating transcript-specific regions, alongside long-read preprocessing and annotation tools.

ranked.headline: Gut microbiome variants, networks and metabolites linked to host phenotype and disease
ranked.summary: Cohort-scale PheWAS, interpretable graph networks and gut-disease databases make microbiome-host links testable and reusable across phenotypes and diseases.

ranked.headline: Generative and structure-based models rank sequence variants and are tested against assays or benchmarks
ranked.summary: Four preprints pair large-scale sequence generation or ranking with yeast assays or fitness-landscape benchmarks, making model predictions checkable.

ranked.headline: Annotation-independent and panel-wide methods recover repeats and divergent gene families across genome sets
ranked.summary: New tools target consistent TE and gene-family recovery across genome panels, while curated databases extend comparative genomic resources.

ranked.headline: Structure prediction and curated data resources converge on peptide annotation and discovery
ranked.summary: New peptide-focused resources span a condition-resolved bioactivity database, NRP comparison software, and structure-based fold annotation of a salivary EV protein.

ranked.headline: New nuclear and organellar assemblies in haptophytes and mosses sit alongside phylogenomics of land plant algal…
ranked.summary: New assemblies of B. bigelowii and W. fluitans, plus a 104-transcriptome zygnematophycean phylogeny, expand genomic sampling across understudied photosynthetic lineages.

ranked.headline: Interpretable models isolate neurodegeneration programs in single-cell and proteomic data
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs learned models with resolved readouts and adds genetic or mechanistic validation to neurodegeneration datasets.

ranked.headline: Tools link biological networks to omics data and Gene Ontology annotation layers
ranked.summary: Three early-November 2026 preprints present R, client-side, and annotation-layer tools for handling biological networks alongside omics and GO data.

ranked.headline: Deep-learning RNA structure predictions tested against experimental and novel folds
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test AlphaFold 3 and deep-learning predictions on novel RNAs and protein-RNA interfaces against experimental structures.

ranked.headline: Provenance-aware LLM agents target bioinformatics and omics analysis workflows
ranked.summary: Expert-written benchmarks now test frontier models on biology tasks, while agent systems add bounded orchestration over provenance-tracked data.

ranked.headline: Correcting covariate and medication adjustment bias in genetic association studies
ranked.summary: Covariate and medication adjustments in GWAS and trio analyses are being corrected at the phenotype, liability, and summary-statistic levels.

ranked.headline: Models couple membrane mechanics and transport to cell migration and invasion
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one publication apply mathematical and simulation frameworks to migration, invasion, and perforated-cell electrochemistry.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models dissect noise in gene expression, bacterial growth, and epidemics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study add exact simulation, growth-rate inference, and noise decomposition for stochastic biological models.

ranked.headline: Network geometry and quantitative proteomics read out functional reorganization in cells
ranked.summary: Quantitative proteomics paired with network-level and transcript-aware computational tools is expanding how molecular organization is read across cellular scales.

ranked.headline: Context-refined methods sharpen regulatory network and kinase activity inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a Briefings in Bioinformatics paper target compact, context-specific gene sets and priors for regulatory inference.

ranked.headline: Learned models rank protein pockets, surfaces, and ligands for candidate selection
ranked.summary: Learned scoring of pockets, surfaces, and binding partners is narrowing candidate spaces before costly experimental or docking follow-up.

ranked.headline: Computational methods replace sequential steps in cryo-EM and cryo-ET density analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study report automated, statistically defined alternatives to sequential cryo-EM and cryo-ET processing steps.

ranked.headline: Controlled benchmarks probe ML generalization for molecular property prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work supplies curated peptide solubility data and endpoint-specific ADMET protocols that enable controlled comparison of molecular property models.

ranked.headline: Sequencing analysis tools are being tuned for speed, memory behavior, and accuracy
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication report large speedups and systems-level profiling for sequencing analysis, alongside accuracy benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and interpretability probe whether DNA models learn real regulatory logic
ranked.summary: Interpretability and benchmarking studies now test whether sequence-based models encode biological mechanism beyond predictive accuracy.

ranked.headline: Validating transcriptomic inferences against confounders and independent readouts
ranked.summary: Transcriptomic models are increasingly tested against confounders, identifiability limits and independent readouts rather than judged on fit alone.

ranked.headline: Grounded agents extend from laboratory memory to autonomous physical execution
ranked.summary: Agentic systems are moving from grounded data analysis and dataset readiness criteria toward autonomous instrument-driven experiments.

ranked.headline: Generative protein ensemble models are coupled to experimental observables
ranked.summary: Four early-November 2026 preprints pair generative conformational ensemble models with SAXS, cryo-EM, and DEER data.

ranked.headline: Cross-cohort transfer and multimodal models for cancer omics prediction
ranked.summary: Cross-cohort validation and calibration checks are becoming the decisive test for transfer-based omics models in tumour prediction.

ranked.headline: Structure-based modelling maps disease variants to hydration sites and protein interfaces
ranked.summary: Structure-based approaches now connect cervid PRNP and human missense variants to predicted condensation signatures, interfaces and conserved hydration sites.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks expose shared de novo peptide errors; MS/MS fragment priors under scrutiny
ranked.summary: A published benchmark of eight de novo models finds shared errors from limited fragment coverage, as new preprints revisit fragment-ion evidence in MS/MS.
